issues.parameter: Orbital eclipse-timing interpretation and period derivative
issues.competing_evidence: Schwarz+09 Table 2a provides poor linear, quadratic (Pdot=-7.3e-12 s/s), sinusoidal (~13 yr), and combined fits; Bours+14 §5.2 gives a quadratic Pdot=-5.2e-12 s/s but rejects the old single-planet solution and finds no unique fit to all data; Schwope & Thinius+18 publisher abstract (full text inaccessible) says the steep 2010-2013 O-C decline slowed before mid-2016. The timings are accretion-spot egress markers and can move with spot/state changes.
issues.why_it_matters: A secular orbital derivative materially affects evolutionary comparisons and a planet/Applegate interpretation is not established by these timing fits.
issues.needed_action: Keep the Bours+14 reference ephemeris period for catalog indexing, but do not use a single Pdot in population analysis until full Schwope & Thinius+18 data/fit context and the timing-marker systematics are reviewed; choose whether population plots should show only P_orb or separately tagged model-dependent Pdot candidates.

issues.competing_evidence: Watson+03 Table 3 prints q=0.25 with M1=0.61 and M2=0.15 Msun, numerically consistent with M2/M1; the paper's method prose defines the opposite convention in one place. §7.2 compares the q=0.25 reconstruction with Heerlein and Schwope values, while Schwope+11 and Schwope+25 explicitly define Q=MWD/M2≈4.6.
issues.why_it_matters: A silently inverted ratio can corrupt binary mass-ratio comparisons and period-dependent donor analysis.
issues.needed_action: Keep Watson's printed q=0.25 and masses as separate historical table values without adopting or inverting the ratio; decide whether the codebook should label its convention unresolved or annotate the likely M2/M1 interpretation.

issues.competing_evidence: Ferrario+15 Table 2 lists BZeem,phot=20: MG and cites Schwope+93a, Schwope+97 and Glenn+94b in the HU Aqr row; the colon marks an uncertain secondary-table value. The primary cyclotron/accretion-region field from Schwope+03 is near 34 MG, and Ferrario+15 separately lists Bcyc1=37 MG.
issues.why_it_matters: Photospheric Zeeman and accretion-region cyclotron fields are different diagnostics; mixing them changes the inferred WD field and population comparison.
issues.needed_action: Locate the original spectrum/source behind the Ferrario+15 20: MG table entry, inspect its component and method, and adopt it only if a primary photospheric field result is confirmed; otherwise retain as secondary-only/unresolved.

issues.parameter: Ridder+23 compiled X-ray flux source-state/spectrum mapping
issues.competing_evidence: Ridder+23 Table 3 gives 3.3e-14 erg cm-2 s-1 (1-10 keV) and 5.4e-14 erg cm-2 s-1 (0.1-10 keV) without per-row uncertainties or an explicit HU Aqr epoch/model mapping. Schwarz+09 reports epoch-resolved unabsorbed bolometric XMM fluxes: intermediate-state soft/hard components substantially brighter than low-state October 2003 and May 2005 values.
issues.why_it_matters: These flux products have different energy bands, state, and absorption/bolometric conventions; substituting one for another can misstate the accretion state or X-ray luminosity.
issues.needed_action: Trace Ridder+23's HU Aqr Table 3 inputs to the exact XMM observation/model and record its bandpass, absorption convention and uncertainty if recoverable; until then preserve compiled and epoch-specific values separately.
